$comment: The canonical scene matrix — C7's single source of truth, read by BOTH the
native SwiftUI harness (Sources/) and the web calibration page
(packages/calibration/scene/). Geometry lives here rather than in either
renderer because the spec's diff is only meaningful when both sides place
the same shape at the same place: 'identical pre-rendered raster
backgrounds so font-rasterisation differences never pollute the diff'
generalises to geometry, and two hand-kept copies of a rect would drift.
All lengths are logical (CSS/point) px; the capture scale multiplies them.

light-solid.$comment: System light grey. The flat case: no backdrop detail, so tint and rim read alone.

dark-solid.$comment: System dark. Pairs with the dark-scheme profiles.

$comment: W7's missing holdout backdrop, and the ONLY reason this background exists.
W7's measured tone-adaptation law is a smoothstep DOWN over a curve
argument of backdropLuminance + 0.09*sizeThickness(span), with edges at
0.14 and 0.02 — so the whole axis lives between those two luminances, and
every backdrop the bed already had sits OUTSIDE that band: dark-solid at
linear 0.0117 is below the lower edge (fully adapted), and every other one
— hc-text, checkerboard, photo, light-solid — is above the upper edge
(not adapting at all). The axis therefore landed with a holdout that
proves no regression and cannot validate the mechanism (W7 Surprise,
2026-08-30: 'a bed gap, not a discipline breach').
Measured, not asserted. Each committed 1x raster's linear-light mean by
Rec.709 — the same rule the runtime samples a backdrop with — evaluated
against the landed constants at a capsule-button's 44px span
(sizeThickness = smoothstep(32, 96, 44) = 0.09229, so the size term adds
+0.00831 to the curve's argument):
impulse         0.003750  ->  1.000000   pinned at the ceiling
dark-solid      0.011711  ->  0.999999   pinned at the ceiling
mid-dark-solid  0.059511  ->  0.650196   ON THE SLOPE
photo           0.214065  ->  0.000000   off the curve
checkerboard    0.500000  ->  0.000000   off the curve
hc-text         0.740031  ->  0.000000   off the curve
light-solid     0.890969  ->  0.000000   off the curve
For a capsule the curve saturates at 1 at or below linear 0.011694 and
reaches 0 at or above 0.131694. Every backdrop the bed had was outside
that window, so every dark cell was pinned flat against a rail and
carried no gradient at all: a refit could reshape the curve freely
without moving a single committed pixel. That is the gap, measured, and
mid-dark-solid at 0.650196 is the one point on the slope that closes it.
A neutral 69/255 grey is linear 0.059511 by Rec.709 — squarely inside the
transition, and far enough from both edges that the size term (up to
+0.09 for a maximally thick span) cannot push it out of the band. Neutral
rather than tinted on purpose: the axis is a function of LUMINANCE, so a
chromatic backdrop would confound the one thing this scene measures.
W27c G1b's missing chroma anchor, and the ONLY reason this background
exists. Same argument, same shape, as mid-dark-solid above: an axis the
bed identifies only where it cannot be isolated, and one purpose-built
uniform patch that puts a point on it.
The axis is CHROMA TRANSFER — how much of a backdrop's colour the
material transmits. Claims §5.134 §3 (c)/(e) classify the inactive
endpoint's two colour residuals as one model-form gap: the reference's
inactive material transmits MORE of a chromatic backdrop's chroma than
its active one, rising with span, and the one declared field that governs
chroma transmission is the body lerp's alpha, which neither scheme's
recede moves. Every chroma observation in the bed today comes from
`photo`, a broadband field whose chroma, luminance and spatial structure
all vary together — so a chroma error there is confounded with a level
error and with the far-span scatter residual at the same time. Every
backdrop that is uniform (light-solid, dark-solid, mid-dark-solid) is
NEUTRAL. The bed therefore has no cell at which transmitted chroma can be
read on its own, and experiment arm A1's (level, chroma) reachability
test is an inference rather than a measurement.
Measured, not asserted. The level is matched to `photo` so that level and
chroma vary independently across the pair, and the hue and saturation are
chosen to be the most chroma sRGB can carry at that level:
photo@1x, mean linear Rec.709 over the canvas   0.214065
OKLab chroma                                    0.3089
OKLab hue                                       318.7 deg
(213, 2, 255) is the integer sRGB triple of greatest OKLab chroma whose
luminance is within 5e-4 of photo's, searched over the whole cube. A
zero-variance backdrop at photo's own level means the untinted pair
photo/mid-chroma-solid differs in chroma and spatial structure and NOT in
level, which is what makes transmitted chroma separable from the level
target the recede actually moves.
The hue is 318.7 deg and systemOrange's is 62.6 deg — 104 deg apart in
OKLab, the widest practical separation at this level. That is deliberate:
the tinted cell here has to separate 'the author's hue survives' from
'the backdrop's chroma is transmitted', which claims §5.134 §3 (e) shows
the checkerboard could not, and a backdrop sharing the tint's hue would
confound exactly those two.
Not a substitute for photo. A saturated patch is where the transfer is
READ; photo is where it has to hold with structure present.

checkerboard.$comment: Spec-mandated. Every cell edge is a step edge, so one capture yields many edge-spread samples for blur system identification.

impulse.$comment: Spec-mandated. A grid of small bright squares on black approximates a 2-D impulse train: the material's response to it IS the blur kernel, and the spacing keeps neighbouring responses from overlapping at any plausible sigma. A literal single pixel is too little energy to measure at 1x.

photo.$comment: A deterministic multi-frequency colour field rather than a real photograph: it carries broadband detail and saturated hue transitions (what a photo contributes to a glass diff) with no licensed asset and no decode differences between the two renderers.

hc-text.$comment: High-contrast text, drawn as GEOMETRIC BARS, not glyphs. Real text would reintroduce exactly the font-rasterisation difference the spec's raster-background rule exists to eliminate; bars keep the high-frequency black-on-white structure that stresses the material's legibility handling.

checkerboard-4.$comment: The finest pitch: below every plausible kernel width, so the material's response to it is flat and the cell reads the passband's far end.

checkerboard-32.$comment: Twice the canonical pitch — the first pitch on which the reference's thick cells read a width above 4 device px, and with checkerboard-64 the fitting ground the heavy share needs.

checkerboard-64.$comment: Four times the canonical pitch. At this pitch the thin surfaces still read 2.00-2.10 device px while the thick ones read 6.00-6.75, which is the separation the wave is fitted on; rrect-sm is 64 px wide and centred, so it lies inside one uniform cell and its reading there is geometry rather than material.

checkerboard-lc16.$comment: The canonical pitch at low contrast. Step height and step pitch are separate axes, and a reader whose residual is a fraction of the step height needs both moved independently to be believed.

hc-text-7.$comment: Half the canonical row height — the legibility case at twice the spatial frequency.

capsule-button.$comment: The canonical control. Capsules are exact in vitrea's field family (S2), so this scene isolates material error from corner error.

rrect-ml.$comment: The band's calibration point. sizeThickness saturates at sizeSpanMax = 96, so every existing calibration cell sits at or below the band's top and the band cannot be identified from them (claims 5.16). Span 128 is the largest this 320x200 canvas carries with the reference's own shadow substantially intact: 36 px of vertical margin against a downward reach of 33-37 px, comparable to the margin-35 glass-over-glass cells whose fitted sigma is within 1% of the unclipped value. Expect the truncation guard to withdraw the downward extent here (clearance 35.5 px against that reach) while sigma and amplitude survive; that is the instrument working, not a defect in the cell. r/min = 0.211 matches rrect-md's 0.208 and rrect-lg's 0.2125 and stays well under Apple's 0.327 saturation point, so corners remain comparable across the sweep (S2). The shadow axis on this cell is marginal by construction and must not be used to fit a shadow constant. Declared without committed fixtures while the stability study runs (claims 5.21): the study publishes no bed, and compare refuses a planned cell with no capture rather than inventing one.

rrect-lg.$comment: The size sweep exists because Apple's material is size-parameterised: a larger surface must show deeper shadow and stronger lensing over the same backdrop (parent acceptance #2). r/side = 0.2125, safely under Apple's 0.327083 saturation point, so these corners stay comparable (S2).

toolbar-group.$comment: Three siblings inside one GlassEffectContainer / GlassGroup — the container-scoped sampling case. Spacing 12 is inside plausible merge distance, so this also shows whether the two implementations union proximity the same way.

glass-over-glass.$comment: S1's mandated scene: an overlay-plane proxy necessarily samples the BASE plane's rendered output, so the overlay's material must be calibrated against an already-glassed backdrop, not raw content. Without this scene the overlay tier has no ground truth at all.

rrect-md-clear20.$comment: rrect-md displaced 32 points down: centred it clears 52 px of canvas on the short axis, offset it clears 20 — rrect-lg's clearance at rrect-md's span.

$comment-probe-backgrounds: Where the probe set's backdrops are explained, and why they cost nothing.
At the ROOT rather than inside 'backgrounds' for the reason '$comment-tints'
is at the root: that map decodes as [String: BackgroundSpec] on the native
side, so a comment key inside it is a phantom background, not a comment.
The pitch ladder and the two extra text scales are W25's, for the `probe`
fixture set (Decision Log 3 (e)). Every one of them reuses a background KIND
this harness already draws — a checkerboard at another cell size, a text-rows
at another row height — so declaring them adds no generator, and the code
that draws them is untouched. They are W9's and W21's grid backgrounds
verbatim (`scenes-w9-probe.json`), moved into the canonical matrix so that
the grids are captured by an ordinary harness run rather than by a
wave-local scenes file read through VITREA_SCENES.
The pitch is the instrument, which is why there is a ladder of them at all.
W25 G0 read the same reference cell at 1.30 device px against the 16 px
checkerboard, 4.75 against the 32 px one and 6.25 against the 64 px one,
where a single Gaussian returns the same number at every pitch: the
reference's kernel is two components, and a reader identifies a width only
up to about an eighth of the backdrop's step. The coarse pitches are
therefore the only fixtures that can carry the thick surface's heavy share,
and at 2x the only ones that identify its width above span 96 at all
(claims 5.113).
$comment-probe-components: W25's four probe shapes (Decision Log 3 (d) and (e)), at the root for the
same reason the backgrounds' rationale is.
The three new spans hold rrect-ml's aspect ratio of 1.75 and its radius
fraction of 0.211 to within 0.003, so the sweep 48 / 64 / 80 / 128 / 160
varies the short side and nothing else — and the short side through a
saturating curve is what W25 G0 confirmed the size law's argument to be
(r 0.95-0.998 against 0.68-0.96 for the long side, area, root-area and
radius, on both the width and the level). rrect-64's radius is 13.5 rather
than an integer because the fraction is the quantity being held and a corner
is drawn from a curve, not from a pixel grid. Three spans cannot show where
the reference's collapse over dark-solid turns on and off; six can.
rrect-md-clear20 is the confound-breaker. On this 320x200 canvas the
short-axis clearance falls with span — 84 CSS px at 32, 52 at 96, 20 at 160
— so 'the collapse keys on span' and 'the collapse keys on how close the
surface is to the window's edge' fit every fixture on disk equally well, and
nothing captured so far separates them. This is rrect-md's geometry exactly,
displaced down the short axis until its clearance is rrect-lg's 20 px: the
span held, the clearance moved.
It uses the `offset` channel rather than a wider canvas because `offset` is
already decoded and applied for a top-level shape on both sides — the native
harness's SceneViews and the web side's placeComponent — while `canvas` is
one declaration for the whole matrix. A per-scene canvas would be a schema
change on both renderers and would re-size the pixel dimensions of every
fixture captured under it.
$comment-tints: W3's author-tint registry — a THIRD axis beside backgrounds and components,
declared here rather than smuggled into either. X2 is binding: new axes
extend the scene set, never the key grammar, so no profile key changes and
the six declared keys capture a tinted scene exactly as they capture any
other. The scene id stays three '__'-separated segments and a tint folds
into the THIRD as a suffix on the state ('rest-tint-orange'), because two
consumers parse that grammar and a fourth segment would be a migration
across four files to express something the state segment already has room
for. Not a new 'states' entry either: a tinted surface is at REST, and
collapsing an orthogonal axis into the state map would make rest x pressed
x tint unrepresentable the moment anyone wants a pressed tinted cell.
A colour's ALPHA is its strength on both sides: SwiftUI's Color.opacity and
vitrea's colour-alpha are the same axis, which is what the -half cell tests.
The rationale lives at the ROOT rather than inside 'tints' because that map
decodes as [String: TintSpec] on the native side — a '$comment' key in it
would be a phantom tint id, not a comment.
$comment-interaction: W27c G0/G1's recovered-inactive-bed axis (claims §5.128; X3, X7), declared here
for the reason '$comment-tints' is at the root: 'interaction' is a plain
string field on a scene entry, not a registry, and would decode as a phantom
scene field if a comment sat inside one.
A recovered scene's 'state' carries activation alone ('inactive'), per
X3 and the 'states' entry above — but four of the 121 recovered fixtures
were themselves captured over a 'pressed' source scene, and collapsing that
into 'state' too would repeat the exact trap '$comment-tints' already names:
'collapsing an orthogonal axis into the state map would make rest x pressed
x tint unrepresentable the moment anyone wants a pressed tinted cell' — here
inactive x pressed. So interaction rides its own optional field, exactly as
tint does, present only on the four scenes it applies to (value 'pressed';
absent means rest). The scene id's third segment folds it in as a suffix
after the state and before any tint suffix — 'inactive-pressed', or
'inactive-pressed-tint-<id>' were a tinted pressed cell ever recovered —
which is the same suffix convention '-tint-<id>' already uses. Every
existing scene is unaffected: 'interaction' is absent everywhere but these
four, and 'pressed' keeps meaning what it always has via 'state'.

orange.$comment: systemOrange. Warm, far from the material's neutral white, and the hue Apple's own tinting examples use.

blue.$comment: systemBlue. The second hue exists to test that ONE tone curve serves every seed; a per-hue difference here refutes the model rather than retuning it.

orange-half.$comment: The strength axis. vitrea reads a colour's alpha as how far the material's tint moves toward the tone, and SwiftUI's Color carries opacity the same way — so this cell checks that the two agree about what half-strength means.

pressed.$comment: Apple's interactive() press response. Scriptable natively by driving the view's press state; on the web by the runtime's pressed interaction state. Motion is C9's axis — this is the settled pressed pose, not a transient.

inactive.$comment: W27c G0/G1 (claims §5.128; X3, X7): the window-recede pose, recovered from the pre-DL14 tree (973fd7e^) where the harness's borderless window could never become key. X3 rules the pose into the scene `state`, never a profile-key segment; it reads bare, per the wave's own worked example (checkerboard__rrect-md__inactive), because activation is the ONE axis 'state' carries for a recovered scene — the same reason 'rest' reads as the unmarked default everywhere else in this file. Schema 2, single run per cell, pose inferred from the DL14 post-mortem — not attested per cell (W27 Decision Log 5). A recovered scene whose source was 'pressed', not 'rest', carries that separately: see '$comment-interaction'.

$comment: The primary profile: every scene. W3's 12 tinted scenes and W7's
mid-dark-solid holdout are picked up automatically, which is exactly
where the tint measurement is sized to live (7 calibration + 2
validation + 3 holdout, all at 1x).
'all' is left alone on BOTH light-standard profiles rather than being
expanded into an explicit list. W3's plan named a trap here — that 'all'
would drag in the dark-scheme and accessibility tinted cells — but the
trap does not arise as built: those profiles capture the SAME scene ids
under a different colour scheme and a11y mode, so there is no extra id
for 'all' to over-collect. What 'all' does add is the tinted set at 2x,
which W3 excluded from its cell BUDGET (the tone map is a function of
backdrop luminance, which is scale-free, so nothing at 2x is fitted).
Capturing them anyway costs about two minutes of one session and buys a
free falsification of that scale-free assumption; pinning an explicit
list to avoid it would instead cost the invariant this file already
holds — that the profiles stay scene-comparable across scale — and would
silently drop every future scene from the 2x matrix.

Wave 1 / G3 adoption: extended past calibration-only so the profile has a declared split (2 validation + 2 holdout; the split is per SCENE, so membership follows automatically). Holdout picks cover the size extreme (rrect-lg) and the stacked case (glass-over-glass) — the families the split comment names as where overfitting hides.

W27c G0/G1 (claims §5.128; X3): the 14 recovered-inactive scenes captured for this profile in the pre-DL14 tree (973fd7e^), listed explicitly because this profile states its scenes rather than inheriting 'all'.

W7 adds mid-dark-solid here for the reason the axis needs it most: W7's law says the scheme sets only the NEUTRAL the adaptation departs from, so the same constants run in both schemes without double-adapting. A mid-band backdrop under the dark scheme is the one cell that can falsify that.

W3 adds three tinted cells spanning the backdrop range. They do not extend the fit — the fit is the 1x light sweep. They answer one question: is the tone curve the same in the dark scheme, where the NEUTRAL tint is a different colour? Phase 1 assumes yes; three cells are enough to see the assumption fail.

W25 adds the whole `probe` set (Decision Log 3 (e)). The dark scheme is half of the amendment, not an afterthought to it: the grids' own reading of the collapse, the two withdrawn fixtures and the dark-solid span sweep all live here, and the set is captured under this profile exactly as it is under the light one. It is listed rather than inherited because this profile states its scenes explicitly, and the invariant that the 2x dark list is the 1x dark list holds.
Wave 1 / G3 adoption: extended past calibration-only for a declared split (2 validation + 2 holdout). hc-text as holdout is deliberate — legibility is the axis this mode exists for.
W27c G0/G1 (claims §5.128; X3): the 9 recovered-inactive scenes captured for this profile in the pre-DL14 tree (973fd7e^).
W3 adds ONE tinted cell. Phase 1 claims this axis touches the tint's ALPHA and not its colour; one cell falsifies that if the colour moves, and a second would measure the same claim twice.
Wave 1 / G3 adoption: same extension as reduced-transparency (the profiles must stay scene-comparable — macOS couples the toggles, so this mode's captures embody both).
W27c G0/G1 (claims §5.128; X3): the 10 recovered-inactive scenes captured for this profile in the pre-DL14 tree (973fd7e^).

W3 adds TWO tinted cells rather than one. Phase 1 collapses the tone range toward the bare seed on this axis (ambientTint: 'reduced'), and whether Apple narrows the range, drops the tint, or leaves it alone is a question about the RANGE — which needs two backdrops to see, not one.

profiles.$comment: Wave 1 / W1: the canonical 2x claim surface, every scene. Captured on a virtual HiDPI display (backingScaleFactor 2); the harness skips scale-mismatched profiles per run, so 1x and 2x keys coexist here. Left as 'all' through W3/W7 — see the 1x light-standard entry for why the tinted set is captured here even though nothing at 2x is fitted.

Wave 1 / W1: the 1x dark subset, at 2x — extended with the same split scenes as 1x dark (G3 adoption; the profiles stay scene-comparable across scale). W3's and W7's additions are mirrored here for that same invariant: this list must stay the 1x dark list. W25's `probe` set is mirrored here for the same reason, and at 2x it is the half of the amendment that buys anything new: the grids as they stood on disk were 1x only, and no fixture anywhere identified the reference's kernel width above span 96 at 2x (claims §5.113). W27c G0/G1's 14 recovered-inactive scenes (claims §5.128; X3) are mirrored here too, for the same invariant — this list must stay the 1x dark list.

$comment: calibration / validation / holdout / recorded. The first three are the
anti-overfitting split. The fourth, 'recorded', means captured, committed
and read by NOTHING: no fit, no self-check, no bound and no claim. It
exists because 'in the bed, in no set' was previously unsayable, which is
how the four pressed scenes came to hold fitted and checked roles they
could not honestly carry (Decision Log 19 ruling 1, claims 5.18): on this
bed the native pressed capture is a byte-copy of its rest twin on eleven
of twelve fixtures, while the web side renders a real pressed pose - so
every one of those cells compared vitrea's pressed render against Apple's
rest render, and two of them sat in 'validation' as copies of
'calibration' cells, where the held-out check could not have failed. They
stay captured because they are the only cells that could ever answer the
pressed question, and the next wave's pressed+motion charter needs them.
The split is declared HERE, as data, and the holdout ids are deliberately
not referenced by any tuning code — C9 tunes against 'calibration', checks
itself on 'validation', and may read 'holdout' only to report a final
number it did not fit to. The assignment is by SCENE, not by profile, so a
holdout scene stays holdout in every colour scheme and a11y mode.
What went into holdout is a judgement, not a random draw: the axes tuning
would most like to peek at. hc-text (the legibility case), rrect-lg (the
far end of the size parameterisation), and glass-over-glass (the stacked
case S1 forced) are each the scene where overfitting would be least
visible and most damaging.
W7's addition (mid-dark-solid__capsule-button__rest) is a holdout for a
reason worth stating: it is the ONLY scene in the bed whose backdrop sits
inside the tone-adaptation curve's transition band, so it is the only cell
that can validate that axis at all. Fitting it would leave the axis in
exactly the state W7 landed in — measured everywhere except where it acts.
Nothing may fit to it.
W3's tinted scenes carry their own 7/2/3 split. The calibration seven are
the backdrop-luminance sweep the tone curve is fitted on (five backdrop
levels for a two-ended smoothstep's four parameters — the fifth constraint
is what makes the fit falsifiable rather than exact — plus one second-hue
cell and one half-strength cell). The holdout three follow the same
reasoning as the untinted ones: legibility over high-frequency content
(hc-text), the far end of the size axis where a size-dependent tone would
hide (rrect-lg), and the second hue at the extreme dark end, where a
per-hue floor would show and nowhere else.
W27c G0/G1's 37 recovered-inactive scenes (claims §5.128; X3) each mirror
their active twin's role rather than drawing a fresh judgement: the
recovered pose is additional evidence about a scene the split already
placed, not a new axis for overfitting risk to hide on. The four whose
twin is 'pressed' land in 'recorded' for the same reason their twin does
(Decision Log 19 ruling 1) — they compound two unattested axes and settle
no fit either way.
$comment-probe: W25's fifth role, declared beside `recorded` on Decision Log 3 (e)'s
ruling. A `probe` cell is captured routinely by the harness and read by
fits and by claims — that is what separates it from `recorded`, which is
read by nothing — and it is NOT a gated set: no adopted bound, regression
floor, conditioning exclusion or cross-tier coherence row is stated over a
probe cell, and none of the gate's cell counts moves when this list grows.
The gate is a claim about the frozen bed, and the frozen bed is the four
sets above.
What is in it, and why each part is here (claims §5.113 for every number):
1. The W9 and W21 probe grids WHOLE, solids kept. Those grids were
rendered by wave-local scenes files through VITREA_SCENES into their
own fixture directories, at 1x only; W23 fitted the rim's law on them
and the ledger cites them, so they are evidence the canonical matrix
ought to be able to state. Captured here they become both schemes at
BOTH scales, which is the amendment: the 2x width above span 96 is
identified by nothing on the bed as it stands, and the coarse pitches
at 2x are the only fixture that identifies it.
2. `impulse` over the four rrects. Reader A resolves the kernel into a
sharp component, a heavy component and a share only on a transmitted
dot, and the bed's only impulse rows are the collapsed capsule and
rrect-md — a share of 0.00 and one span.
3. `dark-solid` at spans 48, 64, 80 and 128, in both schemes (Decision
Log 3 (d)). The reference collapses its 160 px surface over dark-solid
and not its 96 px one, single-state in all seven of the W21 grid's
attested runs; three spans cannot show where that turns on and six can.
Captured under the LIGHT profiles too, where the same question carries
a hundred codes of contrast against the dark scheme's six.
4. `dark-solid__rrect-md-clear20__rest`, which holds the span and moves
the clearance, because on this canvas the two are confounded.
5. `dark-solid__rrect-sm__rest` and `light-solid__rrect-sm__rest`, the
two W21 grid fixtures whose majority byte-state is the W9 LIGHT grid's
file. Both were withdrawn as dark readings; declared here they are
re-captured under the dark profiles at the sitting.
Two rules this list keeps. Scene ids are the grids' own, verbatim, so a
probe row and the grid row it continues are the same string. And W9's rule
that a probe cell whose canonical twin is held out is `recorded` rather
than fittable is kept by construction here: a merged matrix has one role
per id, so no probe id can duplicate a canonical one, and every grid id
that WAS a canonical id (the pitch-16 column, photo's three, hc-text and
the solids over rrect-md) is absent below and keeps the role it already
holds. The cost of that rule is stated rather than hidden: those cells
cannot be added to the dark profiles, because their canonical roles are
gated ones and a new dark row under a gated role would move the gate. The
W21 grid's own fixtures remain the dark reading for them, and the residual
is recorded in the sitting's list.
